transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because you smelled burning rubber before the brush stopped, this appliance presents an active fire hazard. You must not use it again until a qualified engineer has inspected and repaired it. The smell indicates that something was dragging or slipping under load—most commonly the drive belt snapping against a pulley, or a motor winding overheating. While you arrange for an engineer to look at it, do not try to force it back into service. If you are comfortable doing so with the vacuum completely unplugged (or battery removed), you can check if the brush bar is jammed by hair or thread, as this often causes the belt to snap. However, given the burning smell, internal electrical damage is also possible, which requires professional diagnosis. Please contact a qualified appliance repair engineer for a safety inspection and repair.

candidates: Drive belt snapped due to overload/friction (high)
Brush bar motor or thermal cut-out failure (medium)

plan: Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Vax.
The fault they reported is: "brush stopped spinning, not picking up from carpet". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
